 2 students, teacher stabbed at Warrenton middle school 
 By First Alert 4 Staff Published : Nov. 12, 2026 at 8:38 AM CST | Updated : seconds ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WARRENTON, Mo. (First Alert 4) - Three people were stabbed at Black Hawk Middle School Thursday morning, according to the Warrenton Police Department.
 Superintendent Dr. Gregg Klinginsmith told First Alert 4 that a student stabbed a teacher and then two other students inside a classroom before running off around 7:55 a.m. The building was placed on lockdown after the stabbing. 
 The suspect was arrested within minutes. 
 Police described the weapon as having a 4-5 inch blade. Dr. Klinginsmith told First Alert 4 that the school does not have metal detectors. 
 Autoplay One of the students who was stabbed was flown to a St. Louis children’s hospital, and the teacher was taken to the hospital via ambulance. At the time of transport, the Warren County Ambulance District said that both were in serious condition. 
 “We are aware of the incident at Black Hawk Middle School and are prepared to provide care to any patients who may require medical attention. Our thoughts are with everyone affected by this situation,” read a statement from SSM Cardinal Glennon.
 Just before 1:30 p.m., police said the student at Cardinal Glennon is now in stable condition. 
 The teacher was discharged from the hospital before 2 p.m. 
 A second student had “superficial wounds,” according to police. The district’s superintendent confirmed to First Alert 4 this was his son. 
 “He was attempted to be stabbed, I think, in the chest, but was able to dodge the stab,” Dr. Klinginsmith said. 
 All Warren County R-III schools were dismissed around 12:40 p.m. All Black Hawk Middle School sports for Thursday were canceled. 
 Dr. Klinginsmith said that the district plans to resume classes on Friday. 
 “The idea here is we want to get our counseling services to our families as quickly as possible, instead of letting this fester over the weekend,” he told First Alert 4. “So, our plan is to have school.” 
 According to the Center for Education Safety, Missouri’s primary statewide school safety organization and clearinghouse for emergency planning and preparedness, Warren County R-III requested Behavior Threat Assessment and Management Training last spring. 
 First Alert 4 is working to determine whether Warren County R-III has completed the training or if the state is still arranging it. 
 Rep.-Elect Fred Wellman(D) MO-02 released the following statement about the incident: 
 “I was just made aware of the incident at Black Hawk Middle school. I’m shocked by any acts of school violence. We are all keeping the victims, students, staff and their families in our thoughts. We will continue to monitor the situation.”
